finding: Three published AP Calculus AB items assess BC-only content. They are not mislabelled -- they are out of scope for the course they sit in, so no AB topic code can be correct for them. This is NOT a work order D defect: D assigned the nearest valid AB topic, marked all three low confidence with needs_human=true, recorded the runner-up, and surfaced the conflict in open_questions.
evidence: apcalcab-mcq-045 asks for Euler's method ("Use Euler's method with step size 0.5 to estimate y(1)") and its author module tag is topic-7.5. apcalcab-mcq-046 is a logistic model (dP/dt=0.18P(1-P/900)), tagged topic-7.9. apcalcab-mcq-050 is arc length ("length of y=x^2 from x=0 to x=1.4"), tagged topic-8.13. CED topics 7.5 (Euler's method), 7.9 (logistic models) and 8.13 (arc length) are BC-only, and the AB registry at 33b4408b correctly omits all three -- its Unit 7 runs 7.1-7.4, 7.6-7.8 and its Unit 8 runs 8.1-8.12. The author tags cite correct CED codes for the wrong course. The items themselves are internally sound (Euler gives 2.5, logistic max growth at K/2=450, arc length ~2.520 -- all matching the keyed choices).
recommended_action: Product Owner decision: retire these three from the AP Calculus AB bank, or move them to AP Calculus BC where the topics exist. A student practising AB would be studying content that is not on the AB exam. Do not resolve it by relabelling -- there is no correct AB label.

finding: D is the strongest of the four overnight runs. Every stated invariant recomputed true, confidence is honestly calibrated, and its rationales survive adversarial checking.
evidence: Packet identical to Production on 6 of 6 field aggregates across all 241 items. 0 codes outside the closed lists, 0 unit mismatches, 0 title mismatches, 0 invalid alternative codes, correct taxonomy_source_version per subject. All 106 recovered codes equal the parsed author topic. Counts reconcile exactly to the work order: 62/60/51/68 = 241, 106 recovered, 135 derived. Independent corroboration: all 20 items with an explicit author unit signal agree with the proposal, and 118 of 119 Chemistry module unit hints agree -- the single exception (apchem-sfrq-007, module unit-6 vs proposed 9.3 Gibbs Free Energy) is correctly resolved to 9.3 and flagged. Adversarial check on rationales: 44 rows claim an "exact <code> hint in modules/taxonomy_refs" and all 44 codes are genuinely present in the packet's author_signals -- 0 fabricated. Concentration is healthy at 4.9% max (Calculus, 54 distinct codes) and 3.4% (Chemistry, 60 distinct), against the 45%-on-two-codes collapse that sank the original Statistics run. I sampled 18 labels in total (8 recovered, 10 derived) and found 18 correct.
recommended_action: No action. Note that the work order understated one signal: it said modules and taxonomy_refs carry "unit-level node_keys, not topics", but many modules carry an explicit topic-N.N tag. D used these as corroboration rather than recovery, which is the correct treatment, and said so.
